en.dek: Pope Leo mailed a ballot from Chicago for the November 3, 2026 midterm elections, becoming the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. general election.
facts: Pope Leo mailed a ballot from Chicago ahead of the November 3, 2026 midterm elections.
Pope Leo became the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. general election.
The U.S. midterm elections will determine control of Congress.

body: Pope Leo mailed a ballot from Chicago ahead of the November 3, 2026 midterm elections. According to Al Jazeera, the ballot was mailed before the deadline. According to CNA, the pope became the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election.
The vote was cast by mail in Illinois, where Pope Leo holds American citizenship. The Hindu reported that he is an American citizen. Le Monde reported that he voted by mail in Illinois.
The midterm elections will decide control of the House of Representatives and the Senate. According to The Straits Times, the elections will determine control of Congress.
A U.S. judge ordered the Trump administration to cease threats to prosecute election officials. The Straits Times reported that the order was issued on October 31, 2026.
The election has attracted international attention. Times of India, Al Jazeera, and The Straits Times reported on the elections and their potential impact on India's trade.
No official statement has been issued by the Vatican regarding the pope's vote. The Vatican has not released a statement.
en.context: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are scheduled for November 3, 2026 and will determine the composition of Congress. Pope Leo has been the head of the Catholic Church since 2024.
